brief.app_summary: Taiga, an open-source agile project-management web app: an AngularJS single-page frontend (taiga-front) that calls a Django REST API (taiga-back), which stores everything in PostgreSQL and keeps uploaded files on disk.

components.name: taiga-front
components.role: Static single-page web UI, built from the pinned source with gulp and served as files by the web server

components.name: taiga-back
components.role: Django REST API under gunicorn; runs database migrations on start; handles sign-up, login and all data

components.name: postgres
components.role: PostgreSQL database holding all users, projects and items (the data that must survive restarts)

components.name: caddy
components.role: Public web server: gets and renews the HTTPS certificate, serves the UI, static and media files, proxies /api and /admin to taiga-back

components.name: media-store
components.role: Uploaded attachments and avatars on the persistent data disk

brief.topology: One Compute Engine VM (Debian 12 + Docker Compose) with a reserved static external IP. Three containers: caddy (the only public part, tcp 80/443), taiga-back (internal :8000) and postgres (internal only). The frontend is built from the pinned commit and served by caddy. Postgres data, uploaded media and caddy certificates live on a separate 10 GiB persistent data disk (auto-delete off) mounted at /srv/taiga, with a daily snapshot schedule keeping 7 days. A firewall rule opens tcp 80/443 only to this VM. Cloudflare A record <W3_RUN_HOST_LABEL> -> the static IP, DNS only.
brief.resource_rationale: A single small VM fits a small team and is the cheapest shape that keeps all of Taiga in one place. Restarts are safe because the database and uploads sit on a persistent disk that is separate from the VM and is also snapshotted daily. Caddy gets a free Let's Encrypt certificate itself, so no load balancer or certificate service is needed. Everything can be rebuilt from the pinned commits.

heavier_alternatives.why_unnecessary: Adds at least ~10-30 USD/month and private networking; a Postgres container on a snapshotted persistent disk is enough for a small team.
About 18 USD/month minimum; caddy on the VM gets and renews the certificate for one hostname.

heavier_alternatives.alternative: Cloud Run for frontend and API
heavier_alternatives.why_unnecessary: Would need Cloud SQL and object storage for uploads (taiga-back stores media on local disk), plus a load balancer or domain mapping for the custom domain.
Cluster fee and operational overhead are not justified for three containers on one host.
Not part of the two given repos; Taiga runs tasks inline and works without live updates (pages refresh instead).

assumptions: Users are mostly in Australia (from this machine's timezone), so Sydney is the default region
A small team: tens of users, low traffic; one small VM is enough
Public sign-up is open to anyone who can reach the site, as requested
No SMTP server: emails (welcome, password reset) are written to the API log instead of sent, until SMTP is provided
Optional Taiga services not in the two repos (taiga-events live updates, taiga-async/RabbitMQ, taiga-protected) are left out; Taiga works without them

open_items.text: Provider profiles providers/gcp.md and providers/dns-cloudflare.md are not shipped in this package (skills/package-omissions.json); following the generic rules, live evidence and official GCP/Cloudflare docs instead.
SMTP: without an SMTP server, password-reset and notification emails are not delivered. Provide SMTP host/user/password later if wanted.
Upstream taiga-front Dockerfile downloads release 6.10.3 instead of building the pinned commit; the deployment builds the frontend from the pinned source instead.
Without taiga-protected, uploaded attachments are served by unguessable URL but without a login check.
Operator did not answer the optional SMTP and admin-account questions; proceeding with no SMTP and no pre-created admin.

Project has no default Compute Engine service account; <RUN_VM_OR_BOOT_DISK> was created with --no-service-account --no-scopes (it needs no Google API access). Ops Agent logging/metrics are therefore not available.
Fixed deploy/docker-compose.yml: settings override is now mounted at /srv-config and copied in, because the upstream entrypoint chown -R /taiga-back fails on a read-only mount inside it.
Unattributed VM stop (14:39:56Z) and start (14:41:10Z) by <ACCOUNT_EMAIL_011> outside this session, between handoff and teardown; not run by the AI. No effect on teardown.
Local files remain on the operator PC: <WORKSPACE>/app/deploy, src (git checkouts) and this watchover record. They hold no secrets.
